title: TLS 1.3 handshake message framing
summary: TLS 1.3 handshake messages are framed within TLS records (content type 0x16). Each handshake message: 1-byte message type (ClientHello 0x01, ServerHello 0x02, EncryptedExtensions 0x08, Certificate 0x0B, CertificateVerify 0x0F, Finished 0x14, ...), 3-byte length (big-endian), then the message body. Multiple handshake messages can share a record.

structure.meaning: 0x01 ClientHello, 0x02 ServerHello, 0x08 EncryptedExtensions, 0x0B Certificate, 0x0D CertificateRequest, 0x0F CertificateVerify, 0x14 Finished, 0x16 KeyUpdate, ... .
Length of the handshake message body (big-endian, max 2^24-1).
Message-specific content (ClientHello: version, random, session id, cipher suites, extensions, ...).

ext.example_decoded: TLS record (handshake, TLS 1.2 legacy version, 5 bytes) wrapping a ClientHello (type 1, length 1, body empty-ish)
notes: TLS 1.3 handshake messages after ServerHello are encrypted (content type 0x17 application data on the wire, with inner type 0x16).
ClientHello carries: legacy_version 0x0303, random (32 bytes), session_id, cipher_suites, compression_methods (must be [0]), extensions.
Key extensions: supported_versions (0x002B), supported_groups (0x000A), signature_algorithms (0x000D), key_share (0x0033), server_name (0x0000, SNI).
Finished contains a verify_data = HMAC(finished_key, transcript_hash).
0-RTT data is sent in early data (content type 0x17 with inner type 0x17) before the handshake completes.
